dz.s: Shredded flatbread with spiced chicken stew, eaten during religious festivals.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
d: Sauté onions in oil, add chicken, and brown with spices.
Add tomatoes, chickpeas, salt, and water. Simmer until chicken is tender.
In a large bowl, layer torn flatbread and pour stew over it.
Mix and let sit for a few minutes before serving warm.

ao.s: A national dish, rich with palm oil and okra, traditionally served during celebrations.
d: Heat palm oil and sauté onions and garlic.
Add chicken and brown on all sides.
Stir in tomatoes, chili, and pumpkin. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Add okra and cook until vegetables and chicken are tender.
Serve with funge (cassava porridge) or rice.

bj.s: A dish influenced by West African traditions, often served with pounded yam or couscous.
d: Brown chicken in oil. Remove and sauté onion and garlic.
Add tomatoes and peanut butter with water.
Return chicken and simmer until tender.
Serve with rice or fufu.

bw.s: Traditionally made with beef, a chicken version is common at local celebrations and family gatherings.
d: Boil chicken with onion and salt until very tender.
Shred and mash the meat.
Serve with pap (maize porridge) or morogo (greens).

bf.s: Grilled chicken marinated in garlic and mustard, popular during village feasts.
d: Marinate chicken with blended ingredients.
Grill over coals or bake until charred.
Serve with attiéké or rice.

bi.s: Skewered grilled chicken, a staple of Burundian street food and communal meals.
i: 2 lb (900 g) boneless chicken, cut in 1-inch cubes
d: Marinate chicken with spices and lemon.
Skewer and grill over charcoal.
Serve with spicy sauce and plantains.

cv.s: Marinated and grilled chicken, often served during festivals and family gatherings with rice and beans.
d: Mix marinade and rub over chicken. Let sit for at least 2 hours.
Grill or bake at 400°F (200°C) for 45 minutes until golden.
Serve with rice and beans or milho cozido (boiled cornmeal).

cm.s: A luxurious dish originally made for company directors, combining chicken, plantains, and rich tomato sauce.
d: Marinate and fry chicken. Set aside.
Sauté onions, garlic, and tomatoes in oil.
Add spices, fried plantains, and chicken. Simmer until thick.
Serve with steamed vegetables or rice.

cf.s: Chicken in palm butter, reflecting traditional forest-based cooking.
d: Brown chicken in oil and remove.
Sauté onions and garlic, add palm butter.
Return chicken and cook on low until sauce thickens.
Serve with rice or cassava.

td.s: Vegetable stew with occasional chicken additions, eaten in communal settings.
d: Boil chicken in water with salt.
Add vegetables and simmer until soft.
Add peanut paste if desired and cook until thick.
Serve with boule (millet porridge).

km.s: Chicken simmered in coconut milk and spices, reflecting East African and Arab influences.
d: Brown chicken in oil. Remove and sauté onions and garlic.
Add tomato, ginger, and return chicken.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with rice.

cg.s: Made with palm butter and spices, considered a national dish.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
1 cup palm butter (palm nut cream), canned or fresh
d: Sear chicken, cook onions and garlic.
Add palm butter, tomato, and chili.
Simmer until rich and thick. Serve with rice or cassava.

cd.s: Often cited as the national dish, rich in tradition and flavor.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
1 cup palm butter (palm nut cream) or 3/4 cup smooth peanut butter
d: Brown chicken and sauté onion, garlic, tomato.
Add palm butter or peanut sauce and simmer.
Serve with rice or cassava.

ci.s: Spicy stew slow-cooked in a sealed pot, a hallmark of Ivorian hospitality.
d: Combine all ingredients in a sealed clay pot or foil pouch.
Cook over low flame for 1 hour, shaking occasionally.
Serve with attiéké (cassava couscous).

dj.s: Chicken in coconut sauce, highlighting East African coastal and Yemeni culinary fusion.
d: Sauté chicken with spices and onion.
Add tomato and coconut milk.
Simmer until thick. Serve with injera or rice.

eg.s: Layered rice, bread, and chicken dish flavored with vinegar and garlic, traditionally eaten during Eid.
d: Boil chicken with spices until done. Fry garlic in ghee, add vinegar and tomato sauce.
Layer bread, rice, and chicken in a dish.
Pour tomato-garlic sauce over and serve immediately.

gq.s: Prepared with local seeds and spices, commonly served at festive events.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
1/2 cup njansa seeds (or raw peanuts, as a substitute)
d: Toast njansa, grind with garlic and chili.
Sauté onion and tomato, add chicken and spice mix.
Simmer until flavorful. Serve with rice.

er.s: Spicy chicken stew served with injera, closely tied to Eritrean holidays and church feasts.
d: Sauté onions without oil until soft.
Add oil, garlic, berbere, and tomato paste.
Add chicken and water. Simmer until tender.
Serve with injera.

sz.s: A chicken and vegetable stew with curry powder, served with pap.
d: Brown chicken in oil. Add chopped onion and garlic.
Stir in tomatoes and carrots with curry powder.
Simmer until thick and chicken is tender.
Serve with pap (maize porridge).

et.s: A spicy chicken stew with hard-boiled eggs, centerpiece of Ethiopian Orthodox celebrations like Easter.
d: Cook onions dry until golden. Add spiced butter and garlic.
Add berbere and simmer.
Add chicken and cook slowly until tender.
Add boiled eggs at the end.
Serve with injera.

ga.s: Chicken stewed in palm butter, considered Gabon’s national dish and served during family feasts.
d: Brown chicken, set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic, add palm butter.
Return chicken and simmer until cooked.
Serve with rice or plantains.

gm.s: Chicken and vegetables cooked with rice in one pot.
d: Brown chicken, add vegetables and tomato.
Stir in rice and water.
Simmer until rice is fully cooked.

gh.s: A spicy, tomato-based chicken soup eaten with fufu.
d: Blend tomatoes, pepper, onion.
Boil chicken with spices and paste.
Add blended mix. Simmer until rich.
Serve with fufu.

gn.s: Chicken in a rich peanut sauce, served with rice.
d: Brown chicken. Sauté onion, garlic, tomato.
Add peanut butter and broth.
Simmer until thick. Serve with rice.

gw.s: Chicken marinated in lemon and mustard, simmered with onions.
d: Marinate chicken in lemon, mustard, garlic.
Brown chicken, sauté onions.
Add marinade, simmer until tender.
Serve with rice.

ke.s: A Swahili coastal dish of chicken in coconut curry, combining African and Indian flavors.
d: Grill or sear chicken.
Simmer with spiced coconut-tomato sauce.
Serve with rice or chapati.

ls.s: Cooked with maize and local herbs, central to mountain village meals.
d: Brown chicken in oil.
Add onions, garlic, and tomatoes. Cook until soft.
Simmer with water until chicken is tender.
Serve with pap (maize porridge).

lr.s: Stewed chicken with spicy tomato gravy, a hallmark of Liberian home cooking.
d: Brown chicken. Sauté onion and garlic.
Add tomato paste, spices, water.
Simmer until thickened.
Serve with rice.

ly.s: A tomato-based chicken stew served with a dome of barley dough.
d: Cook chicken in tomato-based sauce with spices.
Serve with barley dough molded into a dome.
Spoon sauce and chicken around it.

mg.s: Chicken with coconut milk, a festive dish combining Malagasy and Southeast Asian influences.
d: Sauté chicken, add aromatics.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer.
Serve with rice.

mw.s: A thick maize porridge with braised chicken, central to Malawian daily meals.
i: 2 cups white maize flour (for the nsima)
d: Cook chicken with tomato, onion, and spices.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Prepare nsima by stirring maize flour into boiling water.
Serve chicken over nsima.

ml.s: Chicken marinated in lemon and mustard, widely prepared for social and community events.
d: Marinate chicken in lemon, garlic, mustard.
Grill, then cook in sautéed onions.
Simmer and serve with rice.

mr.s: A poultry version of the national rice dish, served during Friday or festival meals.
d: Sear chicken, then simmer with tomato and vegetables.
Add rice and broth. Simmer until liquid is absorbed.
Serve as a large communal dish.

mu.s: A blend of Indian, African, and French influences, served with rice and lentils.
d: Brown chicken with aromatics and spices.
Add tomato and a little water.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Serve with rice and lentils.

ma.s: Chicken tagine with preserved lemon and olives, deeply rooted in Moroccan ceremonial meals.
d: Sauté onion, garlic, spices.
Add chicken and water, simmer.
Add olives and preserved lemon.
Serve with bread.

mz.s: Chicken marinated in coconut milk and lime, from the Zambezia region, served at communal feasts.
d: Marinate chicken, then grill.
Baste with coconut sauce.
Serve with rice.
Marinate chicken, grill over coals.
Serve with pap and chakalaka.

ne.s: Chicken served with tomato cornmeal, a celebratory dish in rural and urban Niger.
d: Cook chicken in tomato-onion sauce.
Prepare a thick cornmeal porridge (djenkoume).
Serve chicken over porridge.

ng.s: Spicy skewered chicken street food, originating from Hausa culture and enjoyed across Nigeria.
i: 1/3 cup suya spice mix (ground peanuts, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground ginger, 1 tsp garlic powder)
Sliced onion and tomato to serve
d: Coat chicken in suya mix.
Skewer and grill until charred.
Serve with onion and tomato slices.

rw.s: Skewered grilled chicken sold at pubs and market stalls, symbolic of community and nightlife.
i: Fries or fried plantains to serve
d: Marinate chicken in garlic-chili mix.
Skewer and grill over charcoal.
Serve with fries or plantains.

st.t: Chicken with Palm Oil and Banana
st.s: A dish of African-Portuguese fusion, tied to colonial and Creole heritage.
d: Brown chicken in palm oil with spices.
Add banana and cook until soft.
Serve with rice or cassava.

sn.s: Chicken marinated in mustard and lemon, a beloved national dish found at family meals and parties.
d: Marinate chicken in lemon-mustard mix.
Grill chicken, then stew with caramelized onions.
Serve with white rice.

sc.s: Creole-style with coconut milk and masala, highlighting the islands' multicultural foodways.
d: Brown chicken, add aromatics.
Stir in curry powder and coconut milk.
Simmer until tender. Serve with rice.

sl.s: Peanut-based stew served with rice, central to home cooking and communal meals.
d: Brown chicken and sauté onions.
Add tomatoes, chili, and peanut butter.
Simmer until thick and rich.
Serve with rice.

so.s: Spiced rice with stewed chicken, a Ramadan and wedding favorite.
d: Brown chicken, sauté onion, spices.
Add tomato and rice, simmer.
Serve with banana.

za.s: A hollowed bread loaf filled with chicken curry.
i: 1.5 lb (700 g) boneless chicken thighs, cubed
1 loaf unsliced white bread, quartered and hollowed
d: Fry onion, garlic, and ginger in oil. Add curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Add chicken, tomatoes, potatoes, and water. Simmer 35–40 minutes until thick and tender.
Fill the hollowed bread quarters with curry.
Serve with sambals or chutney.

ss.s: Tomato-based stew served with sorghum flatbread, a common celebratory dish.
i: 2 cups sorghum flour and 2 1/2 cups water (for the kisra batter)
d: Cook chicken in tomato-onion sauce.
Prepare kisra from fermented sorghum batter.
Serve stew over kisra.

sd.s: Chicken in a spiced tomato stew, served with fried falafel.
i: Ta’amiya (falafel), store-bought or homemade, to serve
d: Cook chicken in tomato-based stew.
Fry ta’amiya, serve together.

tz.s: Coconut chicken curry of Swahili origin, central to coastal cuisine and family events.
d: Grill chicken, simmer in coconut-tomato sauce.
Serve with rice or flatbread.

tg.s: Grilled spiced chicken, served during gatherings and with akume (cornmeal dough).
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
d: Marinate chicken in spice paste.
Grill over wood fire or oven.
Serve with akume or fried plantains.

tn.s: Chicken stewed in spices and finished in the oven, often served with couscous at holidays.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
d: Rub chicken with harissa and spices.
Sear, then braise with broth and finish in oven.
Serve with couscous.

ug.s: Chicken stew steamed in banana leaves, traditionally served at weddings and festive events.
i: Banana leaves, softened over a flame
d: Wrap chicken in banana leaves with sauce.
Steam until tender.
Serve with matoke.

zm.s: Free-range chicken stewed with tomatoes and onions, often eaten with nshima.
i: 2 cups maize meal and 4 cups water (for the nshima)
d: Cook chicken in tomato sauce.
Prepare nshima from maize meal.
Serve together.

zw.s: Traditional rural chicken dish, commonly prepared for guests and special occasions.
i: 1 whole free-range chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
d: Cook chicken slowly until tender.
Add vegetables and simmer.
Serve with sadza.

af.s: A saffron-infused rice dish traditionally served at weddings and major gatherings.
d: Soak rice in water for 30 minutes. Boil until 70% cooked, then drain.
In a large pot, brown chicken in oil with onions, cumin, cardamom, cinnamon, salt, and pepper.
Remove chicken and set aside. Layer rice on top of the oil and spices, then chicken.
Top with sautéed carrots, raisins, and almonds.
Cover tightly and cook on low heat for 30 minutes or until chicken is fully cooked and rice is fluffy.
Serve with yogurt or salad.

am.s: Reflects the Silk Road’s influence and Armenia’s love of dried fruits and spices.
d: Sear chicken, then remove.
Sauté onions, garlic, and spices.
Add apricots, honey, return chicken.
Simmer until chicken is tender. Serve with rice.

az.s: Chicken stuffed with walnuts, onions, and sumac, especially prepared in the southern regions by the Caspian Sea.
d: Mix walnuts, onion, sumac, molasses, salt, and pepper.
Stuff chicken with the mixture and tie legs together.
Rub skin with oil, salt, and pepper.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 1.5 hours until golden.
Let rest, then serve with rice.

bh.s: A spiced rice and chicken dish deeply rooted in Gulf culinary tradition, often served at large gatherings.
d: Sauté onions and garlic in oil. Add chicken and brown.
Stir in tomato, spices, and black lime.
Add water and simmer until chicken is done.
Remove chicken, add rice to broth and cook.
Add chicken back to steam over rice before serving.

cy.s: Chicken baked with pasta and cinnamon, rooted in Greek-Cypriot Sunday traditions.
d: Brown chicken in oil with onion and garlic.
Add tomato sauce, cinnamon, salt, and simmer until tender.
Add orzo and water. Cook until pasta absorbs liquid.
Serve with grated halloumi cheese.

ge.s: Georgian garlic chicken baked in a clay pot, rooted in the rural mountain regions.
d: Spatchcock chicken, roast until golden.
Sauté garlic in butter. Add milk and salt.
Pour over chicken, bake 10 min more.
Serve hot in clay pan.

ir.s: Barberry rice with saffron chicken, traditionally served at weddings and formal dinners.
d: Sauté onion and chicken with turmeric. Simmer with water.
Cook rice separately. Soak barberries in water.
Fry barberries with sugar and saffron.
Layer rice with barberries and chicken.

iq.s: Chicken and bread stew soaked in broth, a communal dish with ancient Mesopotamian roots.
d: Cook chicken in spiced tomato broth.
Tear flatbread and soak in broth.
Serve topped with chicken and sauce.

il.s: A Jewish-European adaptation that became a weekday staple and school lunch favorite.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) chicken breasts, pounded thin
d: Bread chicken with flour, egg, and crumbs.
Fry until golden.
Serve with lemon and Israeli salad.

jo.s: Jordan’s national dish, symbolizing hospitality, especially during Ramadan and Eid.
i: 2 cups plain yogurt (or 1 cup crumbled jameed)
d: Simmer chicken in yogurt sauce.
Layer rice, chicken, and sauce.
Garnish with nuts and parsley. Serve on flatbread.

kz.s: Traditionally made with horse meat, chicken is used in modern adaptations, served on special occasions.
i: 8 oz (225 g) flat noodles or pasta sheets
d: Boil chicken and slice.
Cook noodles in broth.
Serve chicken and onion over noodles.

kw.s: Spiced chicken and rice with saffron, cardamom, and dried lemon, central to Kuwaiti cuisine.
d: Brown chicken with spices.
Add tomato and simmer.
Stir in rice and steam together.

kg.s: Chicken and vegetables in a savory sauce, served over noodles.
i: 10 oz (280 g) hand-pulled or thick noodles
d: Cook chicken and vegetables in sauce.
Boil noodles separately.
Serve chicken over noodles with broth.

lb.s: Marinated grilled chicken skewers, a common street food and mezze item.
i: Garlic sauce and pita to serve
d: Marinate chicken in the yogurt-based mixture.
Skewer and grill until cooked through.
Serve with garlic sauce and pita.

om.s: Rice and chicken infused with saffron and dried lemon, served during Eid and family feasts.
d: Cook chicken with spices and tomato.
Add rice and dried lime.
Simmer until rice is fluffy. Serve with salad.

qa.s: Slow-cooked spiced rice and chicken, central to Friday meals and Ramadan Iftars.
d: Brown chicken with spices.
Add tomato and simmer.
Stir in rice and cook until done.

sa.s: Chicken cooked with spiced rice and raisins, a national dish served at weddings and major feasts.
i: 2 tbsp kabsa spice blend (cloves, cinnamon, cardamom)
d: Sear chicken with spices.
Add tomato, broth, and rice.
Simmer until rice is fluffy. Garnish with nuts.

sy.s: Grilled chicken with garlic and lemon, a Levantine classic served during festive meals and family gatherings.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb) or 2 lb (900 g) thighs
Flatbread and garlic sauce to serve
d: Marinate chicken with garlic, lemon, and spices.
Grill until charred and cooked through.
Serve with flatbread and garlic sauce.

tj.s: Bread salad with onions and yogurt sauce, chicken often added for celebratory versions.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) chicken, boiled and shredded
d: Fry onions and shredded chicken.
Tear flatbread into a bowl, pour yogurt and chicken mix.
Garnish with herbs. Serve communally.

tr.s: Chicken and vegetables baked in clay pots, a rustic Anatolian specialty served in villages.
i: 2 lb (900 g) chicken, cut in chunks
d: Mix all ingredients in clay pot.
Bake until tender and bubbly.
Serve with pilaf or bread.

tm.s: A version of pilaf served at weddings and family celebrations.
d: Fry onion and carrot, add chicken.
Stir in rice and water.
Simmer until rice is fluffy and chicken tender.

ae.s: Rice and chicken with dried lemon, a dish deeply rooted in Bedouin hospitality.
d: Marinate and grill chicken.
Serve with rice and sauce.

uz.s: Slow-cooked rice with chicken, carrots, and spices, served at family gatherings and Navruz.
d: Cook chicken with vegetables.
Add rice, simmer.
Serve with salad.

ye.s: Rice and chicken layered with spices, served at weddings and large family feasts.
i: 2 tbsp Yemeni spice mix (cumin, turmeric, cardamom, cloves)
d: Cook chicken in spiced yogurt.
Layer with rice, steam.
Serve with salad.

bd.s: Mughlai-influenced white curry, served at weddings and special religious festivals.
d: Marinate chicken in yogurt and onion paste.
Heat ghee and sauté whole spices.
Add chicken and cook slowly on low flame.
Add water, chilies, and simmer until tender.
Serve with paratha or pulao.

bt.s: A spicy chicken stew with garlic and ginger, embodying Bhutan’s love for chili heat and minimalism.
d: Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger in oil.
Add chicken and cook until opaque.
Add tomatoes and chilies. Simmer until tender.
Serve with rice.

in.s: Born in Delhi during the partition, now globally emblematic of Indian cuisine.
d: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices.
Grill or pan-fry.
Sauté garlic and tomato puree in butter.
Add chicken and cream. Simmer.
Serve with naan or rice.

mv.s: Spicy curry usually made with tuna, but often adapted with chicken for special occasions.
d: Fry spices and aromatics.
Add chicken and coconut milk.
Simmer until thick and fragrant.
Serve with roshi (flatbread) or rice.

np.s: A home-style chicken curry with tomatoes and spices.
i: 3 tbsp mustard oil or vegetable oil
d: Cook chicken with spices and tomatoes.
Simmer until thickened.
Serve with rice or roti.

pk.s: Wok-cooked spicy chicken, served at roadside dhabas and weddings across the country.
i: Fresh ginger and cilantro to garnish
d: Cook chicken with garlic and tomato until oil separates.
Add spices and chilies.
Garnish with ginger and serve in wok.

lk.s: Rich with coconut milk and curry leaves, commonly made for holidays and rice-and-curry meals.
i: 2 tbsp roasted Sri Lankan curry powder
d: Marinate chicken in spices.
Sauté onion, garlic, and curry leaves.
Add chicken and coconut milk. Simmer until thick.

bn.s: Javanese fried chicken, beloved in Brunei and eaten with sambal, rice, and cucumber.
d: Marinate chicken with spices and deep fry.
Smash the chicken gently (penyet).
Serve with sambal, rice, and cucumber slices.

mm.s: Burmese coconut chicken curry served with noodles, traditionally eaten during festivals and family gatherings.
i: 2 tbsp chickpea flour, mixed with 1/4 cup water
Sliced hard-boiled eggs, lime, and cilantro to garnish
d: Cook chicken with onion and turmeric.
Stir in coconut milk and chickpea flour to thicken.
Serve over rice noodles with toppings.

kh.s: A traditional fermented fish and veggie stew, sometimes made with chicken in rural households.
d: Cook chicken in a pot with kroeung and prahok.
Add vegetables and enough water to cover.
Simmer until everything is tender.
Stir vigorously before serving. Serve with rice.

cn.s: A whole chicken wrapped in clay and baked, steeped in legend and festival tradition.
i: Lotus leaves or parchment and foil
d: Rub chicken with spices, soy, and wine.
Stuff with scallions and garlic.
Wrap in lotus leaves or parchment, then foil or clay.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 2 hours.
Crack open to serve with rice.

id.s: Balinese ceremonial chicken steamed in banana leaves, often served during temple feasts.
d: Stuff and rub chicken with spice paste.
Wrap in banana leaves.
Steam or slow-cook until tender. Serve with rice.

jp.s: Crisp panko-breaded chicken cutlets over rice with a mild, savory curry sauce. Prep 15 min · Cook 20 min · Serves 4.
i: 1/2 block S&B Golden Curry roux (4 cubes, about 92 g)
1 medium carrot, cut into bite-sized chunks
1 medium Yukon Gold or Russet potato, peeled and cut into bite-sized chunks
2 1/2 cups water (or chicken broth for extra flavor)
Optional extras for depth: 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp ketchup, or 1/2 grated apple
2 large chicken breasts (cut horizontally into 4 thin cutlets)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Neutral oil for frying (vegetable or canola)
4 cups warm steamed white rice (Japanese short-grain or Jasmine)
Sliced green onions or pickled ginger/radish (fukujinzuke)
d: Heat the oil in a medium pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden, about 5 minutes. Add the carrot and potato and stir for 1 minute.
Add the water (or broth) and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat, cover, and simmer 10–12 minutes until the vegetables are tender.
Turn off the heat and add the roux cubes, stirring until fully dissolved. Add any optional extras. Return to low heat and simmer, stirring, 3–5 minutes until thickened. Keep warm.
Season the chicken cutlets with salt and pepper. Dredge in flour, dip in beaten egg, then press firmly into the panko to coat.
Heat about 1/2 inch of oil in a large skillet to 340–350°F (170–175°C). Fry the cutlets 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through. Drain on a wire rack.
Slice the cutlets. Serve over rice with the curry sauce alongside or poured beside, topped with green onions or fukujinzuke.

kp.s: Korean grilled chicken, a rare delicacy due to scarcity, yet known through cultural exchange.
i: Steamed rice and kimchi to serve
d: Marinate chicken in soy-sesame mix.
Grill or pan-sear until glazed and cooked.
Serve with rice and kimchi.

kr.s: Spicy stir-fried chicken with cabbage, sweet potato, and rice cakes in gochujang sauce.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) boneless chicken thighs, cut in pieces
Steamed rice or lettuce leaves to serve
d: Marinate chicken in spicy sauce.
Stir-fry with vegetables.
Serve with rice or lettuce wraps.

la.s: Grilled chicken marinated in lemongrass, garlic, and fish sauce, popular at local markets.
i: Sticky rice and dipping sauce to serve
d: Marinate chicken in herb mixture.
Grill until charred and cooked through.
Serve with sticky rice and sauce.

my.s: Grilled chicken with spiced coconut sauce, a Ramadan bazaar favorite in Kelantan and Terengganu.
d: Blend marinade. Coat chicken and roast.
Baste with coconut sauce while cooking.
Serve with rice.

mn.s: Stir-fried chicken with noodles, adapted from traditional Mongolian stir-fry techniques.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) chicken breast, thinly sliced
d: Stir-fry chicken and vegetables.
Add cooked noodles and soy-based sauce.
Toss and serve hot.

ph.s: Marinated in vinegar, soy sauce, and garlic, a colonial-era dish deeply tied to Filipino identity.
d: Marinate chicken in soy and vinegar.
Simmer with garlic and spices until tender.
Reduce sauce and serve with rice.

sg.s: Poached chicken with fragrant rice and chili sauce, a dish that defines Singaporean cuisine.
d: Boil chicken with aromatics.
Use broth to cook rice.
Serve sliced chicken with sauces and broth.

th.s: Grilled chicken marinated in lemongrass and fish sauce, popular in street food and festivals.
i: Sticky rice and sweet chili dipping sauce to serve
d: Marinate chicken in herb-spice blend.
Grill over charcoal until crispy.
Serve with sticky rice and dipping sauce.

tl.s: Chicken (or fish) in tamarind and chili sauce, influenced by Portuguese and indigenous cooking.
i: Steamed rice and greens to serve
d: Marinate chicken with tamarind and spices.
Sauté onion, add chicken and simmer.
Serve with rice and greens.

vn.s: Caramelized ginger chicken, a southern comfort dish often eaten with jasmine rice.
d: Caramelize sugar, sauté aromatics.
Add chicken, simmer in fish sauce.

al.s: A baked yogurt and chicken casserole, symbolizing Albania's Ottoman culinary influence.
d: Boil chicken with salt until tender. Remove and place in a baking dish.
In a pan, melt butter and stir in flour to make a roux.
In a bowl, mix yogurt, eggs, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Slowly add roux to yogurt mixture and pour over chicken.
Bake at 375°F (190°C) for 45 minutes or until golden on top.
Serve hot with rice or bread.

ad.s: Chicken slow-cooked with prunes, reflecting Catalan mountain cuisine.
d: Soak prunes in warm water. Toast pine nuts in a dry pan.
Brown chicken in oil. Remove and sauté onions and garlic.
Add wine and return chicken to the pot with prunes and pine nuts.
Simmer covered for 30–40 minutes.
Serve with crusty bread or potatoes.

at.s: Crispy fried chicken popular since the Habsburg monarchy, often served at family Sunday meals.
d: Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Dredge in flour, dip in eggs, and coat with breadcrumbs.
Deep fry until golden and crisp.
Serve with potato salad and lemon wedges.

by.s: Though claimed by Ukraine, it was widely adopted during the Soviet era and remains a Belarusian classic.
i: 6 tbsp cold butter, mixed with 2 minced garlic cloves and 2 tbsp chopped herbs
d: Flatten chicken, fill with herb butter.
Roll, bread, and freeze.
Deep fry until golden and cooked through.

be.s: Originally made with fish in Ghent, it became a comfort dish with chicken after medieval times.
d: Poach chicken with vegetables.
Add cream and egg yolks for richness.
Serve hot with crusty bread.

ba.s: A slow-cooked chicken and okra soup, symbolizing Ottoman heritage and special occasions.
d: Cook chicken with vegetables and okra.
Thicken with flour, egg yolk, and sour cream.
Simmer gently and serve hot.

bg.s: A chicken and onion stew enjoyed in traditional Bulgarian homes for its rustic simplicity.
d: Brown chicken and onions.
Add tomato paste, paprika, bay leaf.
Simmer until chicken is tender. Serve with rice or bread.

hr.s: Roasted chicken served with flatbread, traditional in northern Croatian Sunday meals.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut up, or 2 lb thighs
d: Roast chicken until golden.
Soak mlinci in drippings or broth.
Serve chicken over softened mlinci.

cz.s: Chicken in paprika cream sauce, a nostalgic dish linked to Czech family meals.
d: Sauté onion in butter, add chicken, and paprika.
Add water, cover, and simmer until chicken is tender.
Mix sour cream and flour, add to pot and simmer.
Serve with dumplings or noodles.

dk.s: Poached chicken with white asparagus, traditionally served in buttery tartlets for holidays.
d: Make a roux with butter and flour. Add broth and cream.
Stir in asparagus and shredded chicken.
Simmer until thick.
Serve in puff pastry shells or with toast.

ee.s: Chicken rolls filled with mushrooms or cheese, a nostalgic element in Estonian holiday meals.
i: 1 cup shredded cheese or 1 cup sautéed mushrooms
d: Pound and fill chicken breasts with cheese or mushrooms.
Roll, bread, and bake or pan-fry.
Serve with dill sauce and potatoes.

fi.s: Creamy chicken with vegetables, mustard, and dill.
d: Sauté chicken and vegetables in butter.
Add cream and mustard.
Simmer until thick.
Garnish with dill and serve with potatoes.

fr.s: Chicken braised in wine, mushrooms, and lardons; a rustic dish dating back to Roman times.
d: Marinate chicken in wine, garlic, herbs overnight.
Brown bacon and mushrooms, set aside.
Brown chicken, add onion and carrots.
Add marinade and tomato paste. Simmer 45 min.
Stir in bacon and mushrooms. Serve with potatoes.

de.s: Roast chicken with braised red cabbage and apple.
d: Roast seasoned chicken until golden.
Cook cabbage with apple, vinegar, sugar, spices.
Serve together with potatoes.

gr.s: Chicken soup thickened with egg and lemon.
d: Boil chicken, shred meat.
Add rice to broth, cook.
Whisk eggs and lemon, temper with broth.
Stir into soup, add chicken.
Serve warm.

hu.s: Chicken paprikash with sour cream, an iconic dish embodying Hungarian spice tradition.
d: Sauté onions in oil until translucent.
Add paprika, stir quickly, then add chicken.
Cover with water and simmer until chicken is tender.
Mix sour cream and flour, stir into pot.
Serve with nokedli or egg noodles.

is.s: Combining traditional Icelandic fruit preserves with imported poultry dishes.
i: 2 lb (900 g) chicken breasts or thighs
d: Roast chicken until golden.
Simmer rhubarb with onion, sugar, and vinegar.
Serve chicken with sweet-tart rhubarb sauce.

ie.s: A creamy filling wrapped in flaky pastry, common in Irish country homes and pubs.
d: Sauté leeks and diced chicken in butter.
Add cream and simmer until thick.
Fill pastry and bake until golden.

it.s: 'hunter’s chicken' cooked with wine, olives, and herbs, rooted in Tuscany and central Italy.
d: Brown chicken, sauté aromatics.
Add wine, tomatoes, olives, rosemary.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Serve with polenta or bread.

xk.s: Chicken and rice baked in a yogurt and egg custard.
d: Cook chicken and rice.
Mix yogurt with eggs and garlic.
Bake chicken in yogurt sauce.

lv.s: A hearty chicken stew with vegetables, dill, and sour cream.
d: Sauté vegetables, add chicken and simmer.
Stir in sour cream at the end.
Serve with boiled potatoes.

li.s: Chicken in a mustard cream sauce.
d: Sauté onion in butter, add chicken.
Stir in cream and mustard.
Simmer until chicken is cooked.
Serve with potatoes.

lt.s: Baked chicken with dill and potatoes, common in Lithuanian countryside meals.
d: Season chicken with garlic, dill, and caraway.
Roast at 375°F until golden.
Serve with potatoes and cucumber salad.

lu.s: Chicken and herbs baked in a pastry with Riesling and cream.
d: Cook chicken with onion and wine.
Chop and mix with cream and egg.
Bake in pastry until golden.
Slice and serve cold or warm.

mt.s: Chicken stewed in wine and tomato sauce, part of Malta’s rich Mediterranean heritage.
d: Brown chicken. Add onion, garlic, tomato.
Add wine and olives.
Simmer until thick.
Serve with crusty bread.

md.s: A sour chicken soup with homemade noodles and lemon, widely eaten as a comforting peasant dish.
i: 6 oz (170 g) homemade or egg noodles
d: Boil chicken with vegetables.
Add noodles and lemon juice.
Finish with fresh dill. Serve hot.

mc.s: Roasted chicken with herbs and olives, showcasing Mediterranean and French Riviera influences.
d: Rub chicken with herbs and garlic.
Roast with olives and tomato wedges.
Serve with potatoes or ratatouille.

me.s: Chicken in savory sauce, often served during family Sunday lunches and Orthodox holidays.
d: Brown chicken with onion and paprika.
Add tomato and flour to form sauce.
Simmer in broth until thick. Serve with mashed potatoes or bread.

nl.s: Chicken in a mild curry cream sauce, served with rice.
d: Sauté onion, add curry and chicken.
Pour in cream, simmer.
Serve with rice.

mk.s: Baked chicken with rice, a staple Sunday dish in Macedonian homes.
d: Brown chicken, sauté vegetables.
Add rice, tomato, and water.
Bake until rice absorbs liquid.

no.s: Creamy chicken stew with mushrooms and potatoes, rooted in Scandinavian home cooking.
d: Sear chicken, sauté mushrooms and onion.
Add cream and thyme, simmer until thick.
Serve with boiled potatoes.

pl.s: Chicken with buckwheat groats, onions, and mushrooms.
i: Fresh dill and pickles to serve
d: Brown chicken, sauté onion and mushrooms.
Simmer together with groats until tender.
Serve with dill and pickles.

pt.s: Spicy grilled chicken, a signature of Portuguese barbecue with African spice roots.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), halved and flattened
1/2 cup piri-piri sauce (or 4 chilies, 4 garlic cloves, 1/4 cup vinegar, 1/4 cup olive oil, blended)
d: Marinate chicken in piri-piri sauce.
Grill over open flame or bake until charred.
Serve with fries or salad.

ro.s: Chicken grilled and soaked in brine with garlic and chili, tied to peasant and rural traditions.
d: Grill chicken over coals.
Prepare brine with garlic, chili, salt, and water.
Dip grilled chicken in warm brine. Serve with polenta.

ru.s: Pan-fried minced chicken patties from 19th-century imperial cuisine.
i: 2 slices white bread, soaked in 1/3 cup milk
d: Mix chicken with soaked bread and butter.
Shape into cutlets, bread, and fry.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

sm.s: Shared with Italy, this chicken stew reflects rustic mountain village cuisine.
d: Brown chicken, sauté aromatics.
Add wine and tomato, simmer.
Serve with polenta or pasta.

rs.s: Roast chicken with potatoes, garlic, and paprika.
d: Season and roast chicken with garlic and paprika.
Roast potatoes in juices.
Serve with salad.

sk.s: Chicken legs braised with onion, paprika, and caraway.
d: Brown chicken and sauté onions.
Add spices and broth, simmer.
Serve with dumplings.

si.s: Roasted chicken thighs with rosemary and paprika.
i: Roast potatoes and vegetables to serve
d: Season and roast chicken.
Serve with potatoes and seasonal vegetables.

es.s: Garlic-fried chicken, a classic tapas dish reflecting rustic Castilian traditions.
d: Brown garlic in oil, remove.
Brown chicken in same oil.
Return garlic, add wine, simmer until tender.
Garnish with parsley.

se.s: A casserole of chicken breast, bacon, and bananas under a chili-cream sauce, topped with peanuts.
i: 1 1/2 lb (680 g) boneless, skinless chicken breasts (about 2 large)
1/2 cup salted roasted peanuts, roughly chopped
d: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Rub the chicken with oil, salt, and pepper. Bake 20–25 minutes, until it reaches 165°F (74°C). Let it cool slightly, then cut into bite-size chunks.
Cook all 8 slices of bacon until crisp. Drain and crumble.
In the baking dish, toss together the chicken, all of the bacon, and the sliced bananas.
Whip the cream to soft peaks. Fold in the chili sauce, curry powder, and a pinch of salt.
Spread the sauce over the chicken layer. Bake 15–20 minutes, until bubbling at the edges.
Sprinkle the chopped peanuts on top. Serve over rice.

ch.s: Chicken in white wine sauce with mushrooms, reflecting Alpine French-German culinary heritage.
d: Sauté chicken and shallots in butter.
Add Riesling wine and simmer with mushrooms.
Stir in cream and cook until rich. Serve with noodles or potatoes.

ua.s: Breaded chicken cutlet with butter filling, iconic of Kyiv cuisine and Soviet-era celebrations.
i: 6 tbsp cold butter, mixed with 2 minced garlic cloves and 2 tbsp chopped herbs
d: Wrap chicken around butter.
Bread and fry.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

gb.s: Chicken in a creamy spiced tomato sauce, served with naan.
i: 1/2 cup yogurt and 1 tbsp tikka masala spice (for the marinade)
d: Cook chicken tikka.
Simmer sauce, combine.
Serve with naan.

ag.s: A one-pot stew of Amerindian origin, served with fungi (cornmeal and okra).
d: Brown chicken and meat in a pot. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic. Add eggplant and pumpkin. Cook until soft.
Return chicken to pot, add spinach, thyme, and whole pepper.
Simmer for 45 minutes until thick and flavorful.
Serve with fungi (cornmeal porridge).

bs.s: A Sunday staple slow-cooked with onions, thyme, and a rich brown sauce.
d: Season and brown chicken in oil with browning sauce.
Remove chicken, sauté vegetables in same pot.
Add tomato paste, return chicken, add water and herbs.
Simmer 45 minutes until tender.
Serve with rice and peas.

bb.s: Marinated in a blend of herbs and Scotch bonnet pepper, central to weekend family barbecues.
i: 1/4 cup Bajan seasoning (thyme, scallions, Scotch bonnet, garlic, vinegar, blended)
d: Rub chicken with lime and Bajan seasoning.
Marinate for several hours.
Grill or bake until golden brown. Serve with rice and peas.

bz.s: Seasoned with recado rojo and served with rice and beans, the heart of Belizean Creole cooking.
i: 2 lbs chicken, seasoned with recado rojo
d: Brown chicken in oil until dark.
Add vegetables and simmer with water for 30–40 minutes.
Adjust seasoning and cook until thick.
Serve with rice and beans.

ca.s: Introduced by Indian immigrants, it became one of Canada’s most beloved multicultural comfort dishes.
d: Marinate chicken in yogurt and spices. Grill or pan-fry.
Heat butter, add garlic and tomato puree. Simmer.
Stir in cream and cooked chicken. Cook 10 minutes.
Serve with naan or rice.

cr.s: A colorful rice and chicken dish, key to festive and family occasions.
d: Sauté onion, garlic, and peppers.
Add tomato sauce and shredded chicken.
Stir in rice and vegetables. Season well.
Cook until warm and slightly crispy at the bottom.

cu.t: Arroz con Pollo a la Chorrera
cu.s: Cuban-style chicken and rice made soupy, a nostalgic comfort meal.
d: Brown chicken and set aside.
Sauté onion, garlic, pepper, add tomato sauce.
Add rice, broth, beer, saffron. Stir in chicken.
Simmer until rice is soft and slightly soupy.

dm.s: A spicy, tomato-based dish served during independence celebrations and Sunday feasts.
d: Clean chicken with lime juice, season and brown with browning sauce.
Sauté aromatics and add chicken back.
Add water and simmer until tender.
Serve with rice and peas.

do.s: Stewed chicken made with sofrito, a fixture at lunch tables across the country.
d: Marinate chicken in vinegar, garlic, and seasoning.
Brown chicken, then add vegetables and tomato paste.
Simmer with water until chicken is tender.
Serve with white rice and beans.

sv.s: Chicken with onions, often served in pupuserias and during weekend gatherings.
d: Sauté onions and tomatoes.
Brown chicken, then simmer in sauce.
Serve with rice or tortillas.

gd.s: Chicken marinated in curry spices and simmered with vegetables.
d: Marinate chicken in curry, garlic.
Sauté onion, add chicken.
Add tomato, pepper, simmer.
Serve with rice or roti.

gt.s: Chicken in a roasted tomato, seed, and spice sauce.
d: Toast seeds and spices, blend with veg.
Brown chicken, add sauce and simmer.
Serve with rice.

ht.s: Stewed chicken in tomato sauce, served with rice and beans, central to Haitian home cooking and holidays.
d: Marinate chicken in epis.
Brown, then simmer in sauce.
Serve with rice and plantains.

hn.s: Fried chicken served with plantain chips and cabbage slaw, common in street food culture.
i: 2 lb (900 g) chicken thighs or drumsticks
d: Marinate and fry chicken until crispy.
Slice and fry plantains (tajadas).
Serve with curtido slaw and mayo-ketchup sauce.

jm.s: Marinated in pimento and Scotch bonnet, a dish born of Maroon heritage and resistance.
d: Blend marinade. Rub on chicken.
Marinate overnight.
Grill or roast until charred.
Serve with rice and peas.

mx.s: Chicken in rich mole sauce, traditionally served for weddings, baptisms, and national holidays.
i: 3 lb (1.4 kg) chicken pieces, simmered until cooked
2 cups chicken broth (from cooking the chicken)
d: Simmer mole ingredients into a thick sauce.
Add cooked chicken and simmer.
Serve with rice or tortillas.

ni.s: Stewed chicken with rice and beans on the side.
d: Grill chicken.
Sauté onions and peppers, mix with rice and beans.
Serve together.

pa.s: Chicken and rice cooked with a sofrito, peas, and carrots.
i: 1 whole chicken (3–4 lb), cut into pieces
d: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and cumin. Brown in oil in a large pot, then set aside.
Cook onion, pepper, and garlic in the same pot until soft. Stir in cilantro.
Add rice and stir to coat. Add broth, carrot, and chicken.
Cover and simmer 25–30 minutes until the rice is tender. Stir in peas for the last 5 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes and serve.

kn.s: A nod to Indo-Caribbean influence, often featured at festivals and home gatherings.
d: Season and brown chicken.
Add aromatics and curry powder.
Simmer until chicken is tender. Serve with rice.

lc.s: Caramelized and stewed chicken, a Sunday lunch staple with Creole roots.
d: Caramelize sugar and brown chicken.
Add vegetables and simmer in sauce.
Serve with rice and peas.

vc.s: A traditional dish often served with ground provisions and rice.
d: Brown chicken with aromatics.
Add callaloo and tomato.
Simmer until tender. Serve with rice.

tt.s: A signature Indo-Caribbean dish, widely served at weddings, parties, and religious festivals.
d: Season and brown chicken.
Add curry and aromatics.
Simmer with water until thick. Serve with roti or rice.

us.s: A dish rooted in African-American culinary heritage, central to Southern soul food.
d: Marinate in buttermilk.
Dredge in flour.
Fry until golden.

ar.s: Cooked over an open fire in a plow disc, a gaucho tradition in rural Argentina.
d: Heat oil in a disc plow (or large skillet). Brown chicken pieces.
Add onions, peppers, garlic, and tomatoes. Cook until softened.
Season with salt, pepper, paprika. Add wine and cover.
Simmer on low heat for 45 minutes.
Serve with crusty bread or rice.

bo.s: Chicken in spicy red sauce, a festival favorite across the Andean highlands.
d: Brown chicken with garlic. Add onion, tomato, and chili paste.
Simmer with water for 40 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook until soft.
Serve with rice and chuño (freeze-dried potato).

br.s: Chicken and rice cooked with saffron, a rural comfort food rooted in Brazilian farm culture.
d: Brown chicken, add aromatics and vegetables.
Stir in rice and turmeric, add water.
Simmer until rice is cooked. Garnish with parsley.

cl.s: Chicken with peas and carrots in a broth, deeply embedded in Chilean home cooking.
d: Brown chicken in oil, then remove.
Sauté onions, garlic, carrots, and tomato.
Return chicken, add wine and a little water. Simmer 30 minutes.
Add peas and cook until soft.
Serve with rice or boiled potatoes.

co.s: Chicken and potato soup from Bogotá, a beloved national dish with historic roots.
d: Boil chicken with onion, garlic, and salt. Remove and shred.
Add potatoes and corn. Simmer until tender.
Add shredded chicken and guascas.
Serve with cream, capers, and avocado.

ec.s: Slow-cooked chicken in beer and naranjilla sauce, served at special family events.
i: 1 cup naranjilla juice or orange-lime mix
d: Sauté onion, garlic, and tomato. Blend into sauce.
Brown chicken and add sauce, juice, and seasonings.
Simmer until chicken is tender.
Serve with rice and fried plantains.

gy.s: Rooted in Indo-Guyanese traditions, often part of weekly family meals and holidays.
d: Season and brown chicken.
Sauté onion, garlic, tomato.
Add curry, chicken, water.
Simmer and serve with rice.

py.s: Corn pie with chicken, typically served during Holy Week and national holidays.
d: Mix corn, eggs, milk, cheese, onion, and chicken.
Pour into greased dish.
Bake until golden and firm.

pe.s: Shredded chicken in a creamy, mildly spicy yellow chili and walnut sauce.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) chicken breasts, poached and shredded
4 slices white bread, soaked in 1 cup milk
Rice, boiled potatoes, and boiled eggs to serve
d: Blend soaked bread, nuts, and aji paste.
Cook in oil, add shredded chicken.
Serve over rice with boiled egg.

sr.s: Oven-baked chicken and root vegetable casserole, served during birthdays and New Year celebrations.
i: 2 lb (900 g) pomtayer root or taro, grated
d: Cook seasoned chicken separately.
Mix grated pomtayer with citrus, tomato.
Layer chicken and pom, bake until golden.

uy.s: Roasted chicken with potatoes, served with chimichurri.
d: Season and roast chicken with veggies.
Serve with chimichurri.

ve.s: Stewed chicken with potatoes and spices, part of traditional Sunday and festive meals.
d: Brown chicken, add vegetables.
Simmer until sauce thickens.
Serve with rice.

au.s: Inspired by Aboriginal bush food traditions with native ingredients like bush tomatoes.
i: 1 cup bush tomatoes or cherry tomatoes
d: Brown chicken in a pot with oil. Remove and set aside.
Sauté onion and garlic until golden.
Add tomatoes and pepper. Cook until softened.
Return chicken, cover, and simmer 30 minutes.
Serve with mashed potatoes or damper.

fj.s: Introduced by Indo-Fijians, this spicy coconut-based curry is a staple at both weddings and casual meals.
d: Sauté onion, garlic, and ginger.
Add curry powder, then chicken.
Stir in coconut milk and simmer until cooked.
Serve with roti or rice.

ki.s: Chicken simmered in coconut milk and root vegetables, reflecting local island ingredients.
d: Brown chicken, sauté aromatics.
Add coconut cream, simmer.
Serve with rice or breadfruit.

mh.s: Chicken simmered in fresh coconut milk with root vegetables, reflecting island traditions.
i: 1 lb (450 g) taro or breadfruit, cubed
d: Simmer chicken in coconut milk with onion and garlic.
Add chunks of taro or breadfruit.
Cook until tender. Serve warm.

fm.s: A traditional recipe using local greens, often cooked in earthen ovens.
d: Boil chicken with aromatics.
Add chopped taro leaves and coconut milk.
Simmer until thick and creamy. Serve with breadfruit or rice.

nr.s: An imported Asian-style chicken dish often served with rice at home celebrations.
d: Marinate chicken in sauce.
Bake or fry until caramelized.
Serve with rice.

nz.s: Roast chicken with kumara (sweet potato), served with gravy.
i: 1 1/2 lb (700 g) kumara (sweet potato), cut in chunks
d: Roast chicken with kumara.
Baste regularly.
Serve with gravy.

pw.s: Grilled chicken chopped and mixed with lemon, coconut, and onions, eaten in communal settings.
d: Mix chopped grilled chicken with lemon juice and coconut.
Add green onions and chilies.
Chill and serve with tortillas or rice.

pg.s: Cooked in an underground earth oven with root vegetables and coconut milk, served at traditional feasts.
d: Wrap seasoned chicken and vegetables in banana leaves.
Pour coconut cream over.
Cook in earth oven or bake covered in oven until tender.

ws.s: Boiled chicken served with taro and coconut cream, often prepared for Sunday lunch or fa’alavelave (family events).
i: Cooked taro or breadfruit to serve
d: Boil chicken with aromatics.
Add coconut cream, simmer.
Serve with taro or breadfruit.

sb.s: Chicken simmered in coconut cream with onion and garlic.
d: Sauté chicken with onions.
Add coconut cream and simmer.
Serve with sweet potato.

to.s: Chicken baked in taro leaves with coconut cream, cooked in underground ovens for special occasions.
i: Banana leaves or foil for wrapping
d: Wrap chicken and onion in taro leaves.
Pour coconut cream over.
Bake or steam until tender.

tv.s: Local chicken cooked in coconut cream with root vegetables, used in traditional ceremonies.
d: Sauté chicken with onion.
Add coconut and chili.
Finish with lime juice.

vu.s: Chicken baked with yam paste and coconut milk in banana leaves, a national ceremonial dish.
i: 2 lb (900 g) yam or breadfruit, grated
d: Wrap chicken in root starch and coconut.
Bake in earth oven.
